papers.title: Single-Cell and Bulk RNA-Seq Profiling Identifies Cell Adhesion-Related Gene Signatures in Cerebral Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury.
papers.abstract: Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) involves complex secondary damage mechanisms, including oxidative stress, inflammation, and blood-brain barrier disruption, in which cell adhesion-related genes play a central role. Therefore, systematically elucidating the expression and regulation of cell adhesion-related genes (CARGs) is crucial for identifying new therapeutic targets to mitigate inflammatory infiltration and preserve barrier integrity. Both single-cell and bulk transcriptomic data were obtained from the Gene Expression Omnibus database. The single-cell data were processed using S
papers.summary: This study combined single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data from public repositories to identify cell adhesion-related gene signatures associated with cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury. The authors highlight how these genes contribute to oxidative stress, inflammation, and blood-brain barrier disruption, proposing them as potential therapeutic targets. The work is primarily a bioinformatic reanalysis of existing datasets rather than an experimental validation study.

papers.title: Wnt/β-catenin reduces fibrosis and enhances hepatocyte reprogramming during cholestasis independent of Yap signaling.
papers.abstract: Cholestatic liver diseases are characterized by impaired bile flow. Repairing damage and reestablishing biliary function may slow disease progression and reduce complications. The Wnt/β-catenin pathway can facilitate biliary repair during cholestasis through multiple mechanisms. The impact of constitutive Wnt/β-catenin signaling during cholestasis was analyzed using S45D transgenic (TG) mice, which express non-degradable β-catenin. Compared to WT, TG mice had increased inflammation and decreased fibrosis during prolonged cholestasis. Furthermore, TG mice had increased ductular reaction and hep
papers.summary: Using transgenic mice with constitutively active Wnt/β-catenin signaling, this study shows that prolonged cholestasis leads to increased inflammation but reduced liver fibrosis and enhanced hepatocyte reprogramming, independent of Yap signaling. The findings suggest that Wnt/β-catenin activation promotes biliary repair mechanisms that may help slow cholestatic liver disease progression.

papers.title: Fast, flexible analysis of differences in cellular composition with crumblr.
papers.abstract: Changes in cell type composition play an important role in human health and disease. Recent advances in single-cell technology have enabled the measurement of cell type composition at increasing cell lineage resolution across large cohorts of individuals. Yet this raises new challenges for statistical analysis of these compositional data to identify changes in cell type frequency. We introduce crumblr ( DiseaseNeurogenomics.github.io/crumblr ), a scalable statistical method for analyzing count ratio data using precision-weighted linear mixed models incorporating random effects for complex stud
papers.summary: crumblr is a new statistical method for analyzing changes in cell type composition from single-cell data across large cohorts. It uses precision-weighted linear mixed models with random effects to handle complex study designs, offering a fast and flexible alternative to existing approaches. The tool is designed to identify shifts in cell type frequency that relate to health and disease.

papers.title: The spatiotemporal ecosystem of gallbladder cancer: From inflamed areas to invasive margins - Integrating biomechanical injury, the bile microenvironment, precursor lineages, and spatial niches.
papers.abstract: Gallbladder cancer (GBC) is usually described as the end point of chronic cholelithiasis-associated inflammation, and yet this linear formulation does not explain why only a small fraction of people with gallstones develop cancer, why histologically similar precursor lesions follow different evolutionary routes, or why invasion preferentially advances through anatomically and immunologically distinct interfaces. We propose a spatiotemporal ecosystem model that links five domains: gallstones and reflux as precipitating conditions; bile as a chemically active habitat; resident or transient micro
papers.summary: This review proposes a spatiotemporal ecosystem model for gallbladder cancer that integrates five interconnected domains: gallstone/reflux injury, the bile microenvironment, precursor cell lineages, spatial immune niches, and invasive margins. It argues that the linear gallstone-to-cancer narrative fails to explain why only a minority of gallstone patients develop cancer and why histologically similar precursors diverge evolutionarily. The framework emphasizes biomechanical injury and anatomically distinct interfaces as drivers of invasion.

papers.title: Integrative transcriptomic analysis links epithelial PCK1 dysregulation to ulcerative colitis and acetyl-l-carnitine-mediated inflammatory modulation.
papers.abstract: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is a chronic inflammatory disorder characterized by persistent mucosal injury and disturbed immune-metabolic homeostasis. Increasing evidence indicates that metabolic remodeling of intestinal epithelial cells contributes to UC-associated inflammation; however, the key metabolic regulators involved in this process remain poorly characterized.
papers.summary: This study uses integrative transcriptomic analysis to identify epithelial PCK1 dysregulation as a key metabolic regulator linked to ulcerative colitis, and shows that acetyl-l-carnitine can modulate the associated inflammatory response. The findings suggest a metabolic-immune axis in intestinal epithelial cells that could be targeted therapeutically in UC.

papers.title: Decoding Skeletal Biology Through Transcriptomics: Insights from Bulk, Single-Cell, Spatial, and Multi-Omics Approaches.
papers.abstract: Transcriptomic technologies have revolutionized our understanding of skeletal biology by shifting research from descriptive cellular characterization to a systems-level analysis of bone homeostasis and pathology. The rapid evolution of bulk RNA sequencing (bulk RNA-seq), single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), spatial transcriptomics, and integrative multi-omics approaches has enabled unprecedented resolution of the molecular and cellular complexity of the skeletal microenvironment. Bone remodeling is a tightly regulated process driven by coordinated interactions among bone marrow-derived mese
papers.summary: This review surveys how transcriptomic technologies—bulk RNA-seq, single-cell RNA-seq, spatial transcriptomics, and multi-omics integration—have advanced the study of skeletal biology, moving the field from descriptive cell characterization to systems-level analysis of bone homeostasis and disease. It highlights how these approaches resolve the molecular and cellular complexity of the bone microenvironment and the coordinated interactions driving bone remodeling.

papers.title: Next-Generation Biomarkers and Artificial Intelligence in Colorectal Cancer: From Multi-Omic Data Integration to Clinical Application.
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, although advances in molecular profiling and artificial intelligence (AI) are now reshaping precision oncology in ways that promise better patient outcomes. This review synthesises contemporary evidence on next-generation biomarkers and AI applications in CRC across multi-omic data integration, liquid biopsy, computational pathology, radiomics and clinical implementation. Several findings stand out. Integrated multi-omic approaches combining genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics and microbiomic
papers.summary: This review synthesizes current evidence on next-generation biomarkers and artificial intelligence applications in colorectal cancer, covering multi-omic data integration, liquid biopsy, computational pathology, and radiomics. It highlights how combining genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, and microbiome data with AI is reshaping precision oncology for CRC. The paper also discusses challenges and pathways toward clinical implementation.

papers.title: Multi-Omics Analysis Identifies TTYH3 and MPG as Candidate Osteoporosis-Associated Biomarkers in Osteoblasts and Characterizes Spatial Heterogeneity of SPP1 in the Osteoporotic Bone Microenvironment.
papers.abstract: Background: Osteoporosis (OP) arises from dysregulated bone metabolism driven by genetic and epigenetic factors. Osteoblasts are central to bone formation, and their functional heterogeneity-shaped by genetic background and receptor expression profiles-may critically influence OP susceptibility. This study aimed to identify osteoblast-specific genes robustly associated with OP and elucidate their underlying pathogenic mechanisms. Methods: We analyzed single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), bulk RNA sequencing (bulk RNA-seq), and spatial transcriptomics (ST) datasets of osteoblasts. Differentia
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell RNA-seq, bulk RNA-seq, and spatial transcriptomics to identify osteoblast-specific genes associated with osteoporosis. The authors nominate TTYH3 and MPG as candidate biomarkers and characterize spatial heterogeneity of SPP1 within the osteoporotic bone microenvironment. The work highlights how osteoblast functional heterogeneity may contribute to osteoporosis susceptibility.

papers.title: Multi-Omics Integration Identifies Epithelial-Stromal-Immune Co-Regulators Bridging Ulcerative Colitis and Colorectal Cancer.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Patients with ulcerative colitis (UC) carry a substantially elevated risk of developing colorectal cancer (CRC); yet, the transcriptional intermediates that bridge chronic mucosal inflammation and colorectal malignancy remain poorly characterized. A related question is whether any genes shared between the two conditions actually help drive transformation, or whether they represent downstream responders. Methods: We integrated two UC microarray cohorts (totalling 227 samples) and the TCGA-COAD dataset (n = 524), combining weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCN
papers.summary: This study integrates transcriptomic data from ulcerative colitis (UC) cohorts and colorectal cancer (CRC) samples using weighted gene co-expression network analysis to identify shared epithelial-stromal-immune gene modules that may link chronic inflammation to malignancy. The authors pinpoint co-regulatory genes that could serve as transcriptional intermediates in the UC-to-CRC transition, distinguishing potential drivers from downstream responders. These findings suggest candidate biomarkers or therapeutic targets bridging inflammatory bowel disease and colorectal cancer.

papers.title: Spatially resolved multimodal hallmarks of response to neoadjuvant immunotherapies in the melanoma ecosystem in 2D and 3D.
papers.abstract: Neoadjuvant immunotherapy has transformed cancer treatment, yet the spatial molecular architecture governing response and resistance across distinct immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) regimens remains poorly defined. We assembled the largest neoadjuvant ICB (NICB) spatial multi-omics cohort to date, profiling over 112 million cells at single-cell resolution across three melanoma ICB regimens using MERFISH spatial transcriptomics, multiplexed immunofluorescence, and scRNA-sequencing. These analyses revealed the full multicellular spatial architecture of the NICB tumor microenvironment, including
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study assembled the largest spatial multi-omics cohort of neoadjuvant immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) in melanoma, profiling over 112 million cells across three treatment regimens using MERFISH, multiplexed immunofluorescence, and scRNA-seq. It maps the multicellular spatial architecture of the tumor microenvironment in 2D and 3D, identifying spatially resolved molecular hallmarks associated with response and resistance to immunotherapy.

papers.title: A Real-Data-Driven Framework for Evaluating Differential Transcript Usage Methods Across Long-Read Bulk, Single-Cell, and Spatial Transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Differential transcript usage (DTU) analysis reveals transcript-level regulation in alternative splicing. With the rapid adoption of long-read sequencing in bulk, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomics, reliable evaluation of DTU methods under real biological conditions becomes essential. Current evaluation frameworks mainly rely on simulated data, which can introduce bias and may not reflect true regulatory mechanisms. A real-data-driven framework is constructed to evaluate DTU methods across long-read bulk, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomics. The framework includes two key components
papers.summary: This paper introduces a real-data-driven framework for benchmarking differential transcript usage (DTU) detection methods across long-read bulk, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomics. Unlike prior evaluations that rely on simulated data, it uses real biological datasets to assess method reliability under genuine regulatory conditions. The framework aims to guide researchers in selecting appropriate DTU tools for different long-read sequencing contexts.

papers.title: From Glycan Biology to Drug Candidates: An Integrated Sialylation Niche Index and AI-Guided Therapeutic Framework for Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Background: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) responds poorly (<20%) to immune checkpoint blockade. Since sialylation suppresses anti-tumour immunity through Siglec signalling independently of the PD-L1/PD-1 axis, we mapped its prognostic landscape in HNSCC by integrating prognostic modelling, molecular subtyping, and AI-guided drug discovery. Methods: Transcriptomic data from seven GEO cohorts and TCGA-HNSC (n = 501) were analysed with a 1204-gene sialylation compendium. The Sialylation Niche Index (SNI) was built in TCGA-HNSC from 117 machine-learning algorithm combinations (nomi
papers.summary: This study integrates transcriptomic data from multiple HNSCC cohorts to build a Sialylation Niche Index (SNI), a prognostic model based on sialylation-related genes, and uses AI-guided drug discovery to identify potential therapeutic candidates targeting sialylation. The work links glycan biology to clinical outcomes and proposes a framework for developing drugs that could overcome immune checkpoint blockade resistance in head and neck cancer.

papers.title: Genotype-driven tumor ecosystems drive immune evasion and immunotherapy resistance in melanoma.
papers.abstract: Genetic and transcriptional alterations in cancer cells shape their interactions with immune and stromal compartments, thereby influencing tumor progression, immune evasion, and response to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). Yet, how these interactions are spatially organized within melanoma and how they relate to clinical outcome remains incompletely understood.
papers.summary: This study investigates how genetic and transcriptional alterations in melanoma cells shape their spatial interactions with immune and stromal cells, and how these interactions drive immune evasion and resistance to immune checkpoint inhibitors. By mapping the spatial organization of tumor ecosystems, the authors link genotype-driven ecosystem states to clinical outcomes, offering a framework for understanding immunotherapy resistance.

papers.title: Characterization of Resolved, Localized, and Progressing Infections at the Maternal-Fetal Interface in a Nonhuman Primate Model.
papers.abstract: Inflammation and infection are responsible for the majority of early preterm births. Host innate immune responses at the maternal-fetal interface that contribute to sterile intra-amniotic inflammation (SIAI), bacterial clearance, or invasive infection remain poorly understood. Group B Streptococcus ( Streptococcus agalactiae ) is a leading cause of preterm birth, stillbirth, and invasive neonatal disease.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study uses a nonhuman primate model to characterize how innate immune responses at the maternal-fetal interface differ between resolved, localized, and progressing infections, focusing on Group B Streptococcus as a leading cause of preterm birth. The findings aim to clarify which host responses contribute to bacterial clearance versus sterile intra-amniotic inflammation or invasive infection.

papers.title: Machine learning-based identification of core regulatory targets in 1-nitropyrene-induced placental trophoblast dysfunction and FGR.
papers.abstract: 1-NP (1-Nitropyrene), a nitrated polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon derived from diesel combustion, is a widespread environmental pollutant with potential reproductive toxicity. However, its role in FGR (fetal growth restriction) and the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Our in vivo results revealed that 1-NP exposure leads to FGR and placental damage in mice, marked by reduced fetal and placental weights, and altered labyrinthine morphology. Integration of scRNA-seq (single-cell RNA sequencing) and bulk RNA-seq data using the Scissor algorithm identified EVTs (extravillous trophoblasts) as t
papers.summary: This study shows that exposure to the environmental pollutant 1-nitropyrene causes fetal growth restriction and placental damage in mice, with extravillous trophoblasts identified as a key vulnerable cell type. By integrating single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing with machine learning, the authors pinpoint core regulatory targets underlying trophoblast dysfunction, offering mechanistic insight into how pollution may drive adverse pregnancy outcomes.

papers.title: Cell-type-specific circadian and light-responsive transcriptional dynamics in adult Drosophila neurons.
papers.abstract: The Drosophila adult central brain contains 240 circadian neurons, of which there are more than 25 different neuron subtypes based on connectomic data. Recent single-cell RNA-seq characterization of these neurons "around the clock" also indicates a similar number of molecular subtypes of circadian neurons, but other conclusions from these transcriptomic studies warranted verifying and extending with other approaches. To address these limitations, we used three complementary approaches: 1) We used a genetic multiplexing strategy to profile the transcriptomes of circadian neurons from multiple t
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
papers.summary: This study uses a genetic multiplexing strategy combined with single-cell RNA-seq to profile the transcriptomes of circadian neurons in the adult Drosophila brain across the day. It reveals cell-type-specific circadian and light-responsive transcriptional dynamics among the ~240 circadian neurons and their molecular subtypes, providing a more robust characterization than prior scRNA-seq studies.

papers.title: Integrative Single-Cell, Spatial, and Bulk Transcriptomics Characterizes an Outcome-Associated, Spatially Organized Mesenchymal Program in IDH-Mutant Glioma.
papers.abstract: IDH-mutant gliomas show variable clinical behavior that may reflect transcriptional programs organized within tumor tissue. We evaluated two curated expression scores: a differentiation-loss/Stem-NPC score (Axis1) and a mesenchymal-hypoxia score (Axis2). Public single-cell RNA-sequencing data were used to characterize malignant-cell states, and the scores were evaluated in bulk clinical cohorts using portable within-sample ranks and covariate-adjusted Cox models. Axis2 was separated into non-overlapping mesenchymal-only and hypoxia-only components. Spatial organization was tested in Visium sec
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell, spatial, and bulk transcriptomics to identify a mesenchymal-hypoxia transcriptional program in IDH-mutant gliomas that is spatially organized within tumor tissue and associated with patient outcomes. By separating the program into distinct mesenchymal and hypoxia components, the authors show that the mesenchymal component in particular tracks with clinical outcome. The work suggests that spatial organization of malignant cell states contributes to the variable behavior of these tumors.

papers.title: Layer-Resolved Spatial Transcriptomic Profiling Reveals Distinct Fibrotic and Muscularizing Submucosal Niches in Fibrostenotic Crohn's Disease.
papers.abstract: Fibrostenotic stricture is a severe complication of Crohn's disease (CD) that affect up to 50% of patients over their lifetime, causing irreversible narrowing of the intestinal lumen and bowel obstruction, but the molecular programs that distinguish stenotic from non-stenotic inflammation and the relative contributions of fibrosis and smooth-muscle remodeling remain incompletely characterized. We aimed to dissect bowel-wall compartment-specific and histology-defined remodeling programs in fibrostenotic CD.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: This preprint uses layer-resolved spatial transcriptomics to dissect the bowel wall in fibrostenotic Crohn's disease, identifying distinct submucosal niches characterized by either fibrotic or muscularizing remodeling programs. The work distinguishes molecular features of stenotic versus non-stenotic inflammation and clarifies the relative contributions of fibrosis and smooth-muscle remodeling to stricture formation.

papers.title: Longitudinal single-cell and spatial transcriptomics reveals intratumor heterogeneity, therapeutic response, and comparative value of canine marginal zone lymphoma.
papers.abstract: Diffuse B-cell lymphomas are the most prevalent canine hematologic malignancies, and their clinical presentation resembles that of human B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphomas (NHLs). However, a lack of a clear subtyping framework perpetuates imprecise treatment approaches that fail to address mechanisms of therapy resistance. Here, we employed deep phenotyping via serial sampling and longitudinal transcriptomics to evaluate intratumoral composition and therapy response in a 6-year-old neutered male goldendoodle with stage 5A marginal zone lymphoma (MZL). Following sequential treatment consisting of a s
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study uses longitudinal single-cell and spatial transcriptomics to deeply profile a single dog with marginal zone lymphoma, tracking intratumor heterogeneity and therapeutic response over the course of treatment. It demonstrates the feasibility of serial, high-resolution profiling in canine lymphoma and draws comparisons to human B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphomas, suggesting dogs may serve as a translational model.

papers.title: An eicosanoid-enriched follicular microenvironment shapes germinal centre immune dynamics in antiretroviral-treated PLWH.
papers.abstract: Delineating the follicular (F) cellular and molecular landscape in HIV infection is essential for understanding neutralizing antibody responses and HIV reservoir maintenance. Multiplex imaging analysis revealed a less differentiated profile for follicular helper CD4 T cells (T FH ) and significantly increased follicular CD25 lo/hi Foxp3 hi T cells in lymph nodes (LNs) from antiretroviral treated (cART) compared to viremic (Vir) people living with HIV (PLWH). Spatial transcriptomics identified distinct inflammatory follicular microenvironments in Vir and cART LNs, characterized by interferon an
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study uses multiplex imaging and spatial transcriptomics to map the follicular immune landscape in lymph nodes of people living with HIV, comparing antiretroviral-treated (cART) and viremic individuals. It finds that cART-treated lymph nodes show less differentiated follicular helper T cells, increased regulatory T cells, and distinct inflammatory microenvironments enriched in eicosanoids, which may influence germinal center dynamics and antibody responses.

papers.title: Microenvironmental and transcriptional determinants of the robustness of spinal cord regeneration in zebrafish.
papers.abstract: Unlike mammals, adult zebrafish can regenerate spinal cord tissue after complete transection. We report here that a substantial proportion of zebrafish receiving this injury fail to regain locomotor function, and we analyzed this critically. After stratifying large cohorts of injured animals according to functional recovery, we directly compared recovered and non-recovered individuals at matched post-injury stages. We find that permanently paralyzed animals form a tissue bridge across the lesion yet exhibit impaired axonal invasion and regrowth to downstream targets. Integrative single-nucleus
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study shows that adult zebrafish, which are generally thought to fully regenerate spinal cord after complete transection, actually exhibit variable recovery, with a substantial fraction remaining permanently paralyzed. By comparing recovered and non-recovered individuals at matched post-injury stages, the authors find that non-recovered fish still form a tissue bridge across the lesion but fail to support axonal invasion and regrowth to downstream targets, implicating microenvironmental and transcriptional determinants of regenerative robustness.

papers.title: Multiscale Transcriptomic and Molecular Modeling Analyses Suggest DCPMU-Associated Epithelial Remodeling and Tumor Microenvironment Perturbation in Prostate Cancer.
papers.abstract: DCPMU, a major demethylated metabolite of diuron, is an environmentally persistent contaminant with potential endocrine-disrupting and carcinogenic relevance, yet its mechanistic association with prostate cancer remains unclear. This study investigated DCPMU-related mechanisms in prostate cancer by integrating network toxicology, molecular modeling, bulk transcriptomics, single-cell and spatial transcriptomics, and virtual perturbation analysis. Differentially expressed genes from TCGA-PRAD were intersected with DCPMU-associated and prostate cancer-related targets. Functional enrichment, machi
papers.summary: This study integrates network toxicology, molecular modeling, bulk and single-cell/spatial transcriptomics to investigate how DCPMU, a persistent environmental metabolite of the herbicide diuron, may contribute to prostate cancer. The authors identify DCPMU-associated gene signatures linked to epithelial remodeling and tumor microenvironment perturbation, suggesting a mechanistic link between this contaminant and prostate cancer progression.

papers.title: Disentangling covariate effects on single-cell-resolved epigenomes with DeepDive.
papers.abstract: Understanding the effects of individual biological factors from single-cell-resolved epigenomic data is hindered by multicollinearity, particularly in human cohorts. We introduce DeepDive, a deep-learning framework designed to systematically disentangle known and unknown sources of variation in single-nucleus ATAC-seq data. DeepDive accurately reconstructs chromatin accessibility, outperforms state-of-the-art methods with incomplete covariate information, and robustly recovers true biological signals from even highly entangled covariates, unlocking counterfactual, "what-if," analyses. Applying
papers.summary: DeepDive is a deep-learning framework that disentangles the effects of individual biological factors from single-nucleus ATAC-seq data, addressing the problem of multicollinearity in human cohort studies. It accurately reconstructs chromatin accessibility, outperforms existing methods when covariate information is incomplete, and enables counterfactual 'what-if' analyses by recovering true biological signals from entangled covariates.

papers.title: OscillomeR infers ultradian oscillations and targets of the Hes family.
papers.abstract: The Hes family, basic-helix-loop-helix transcription factors and downstream effectors of Notch signaling, regulate the fate choices of pancreatic progenitors, muscle stem cells, neuronal progenitors, and presomitic mesoderm cells. Bioluminescence imaging (BLI) has revealed ultradian oscillatory dynamics of Hes-family members Hes1, Hes5, and Hes7. However, identifying which of the Hes target genes also oscillate remains challenging due to the time-consuming and costly nature of tracking individual target genes using BLI. Here, we propose OscillomeR, a computational framework that reconstructs u
papers.summary: OscillomeR is a computational framework that infers ultradian oscillatory dynamics of Hes-family transcription factors and predicts which of their target genes also oscillate, bypassing the need for costly bioluminescence imaging of each gene. It leverages existing expression data to reconstruct oscillatory networks downstream of Notch signaling, offering a scalable way to study Hes-driven dynamics in progenitors and stem cells.

papers.title: Disagreement-informed arbitration for gene regulatory network inference: A score-level meta-classifier and a diagnostic typology of inter-method conflict.
papers.abstract: Gene regulatory network inference methods routinely disagree about individual edges, and practitioners resolve those conflicts by choosing one method or averaging them all. We ask whether the conflict can instead be arbitrated per edge. A gradient-boosted classifier is trained on the raw scores that ten inference methods-correlation-based, information-theoretic, sparse-regression and tree-ensemble, including GENIE3, GRNBoost2, CLR and ARACNe-assign to each candidate regulator-target pair, so that the weight given to each method varies from edge to edge. Across six single-cell perturbation scre
papers.summary: This paper introduces a per-edge arbitration approach for gene regulatory network inference, using a gradient-boosted meta-classifier trained on the raw scores from ten different inference methods (including GENIE3, GRNBoost2, CLR, and ARACNe). Instead of choosing one method or averaging all, the classifier learns edge-specific weights, and the authors also provide a diagnostic typology of inter-method conflicts. The approach is evaluated across six single-cell perturbation screens.

papers.title: Deep Learning-Assisted Prioritization of Candidate Drug Targets in Tumors Using Spatial Multi-Omics.
papers.abstract: Tumor heterogeneity is reflected in cell composition, molecular states, spatial distribution, and microenvironment interactions. Spatial transcriptomics can map in situ expression and cell states but cannot fully explain upstream regulation, while spatial epigenomics provides complementary evidence such as chromatin accessibility, histone modifications, and deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) methylation. This review summarizes the applications of spatial multi-omics and deep learning in prioritizing candidate drug targets in tumors.
papers.summary: This review discusses how combining spatial transcriptomics and spatial epigenomics with deep learning can improve the identification of candidate drug targets in tumors. It argues that spatial multi-omics captures tumor heterogeneity and microenvironment interactions that single-modality approaches miss, while deep learning helps prioritize the most promising targets from these complex datasets.

papers.title: Ferroptosis Signatures in Diabetic Cardiomyopathy: Multi-Omics Discovery and Validation of ACOT1 and TXNIP.
papers.abstract: Background: Diabetic cardiomyopathy (DCM) is a serious cardiovascular complication specific to diabetes mellitus, with rising global prevalence. Ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death driven by lethal lipid peroxidation, has been implicated in the pathogenesis of DCM. However, the key regulatory genes remain poorly characterized. This study aimed to identify and validate ferroptosis-related signature genes in DCM. Methods: Three murine transcriptomic datasets (GSE123975, GSE155377, and GSE210611) were retrieved from GEO and merged after batch correction. Differentially exp
papers.summary: This study integrated three murine transcriptomic datasets to identify ferroptosis-related genes involved in diabetic cardiomyopathy, pinpointing ACOT1 and TXNIP as key signature genes. The findings were validated across datasets, suggesting these genes as potential biomarkers or therapeutic targets for DCM.

papers.title: Integrating Next-Generation Reproductive Organoids with Genomics, Multi-Omics and Bioengineering to Understand Human Infertility.
papers.abstract: Infertility affects approximately one in six individuals worldwide and is a highly heterogeneous disorder resulting from the complex interplay of genetic, epigenetic, endocrine, environmental and lifestyle factors. Although numerous genes and molecular pathways involved in female and male infertility have been identified, elucidating the functional consequences of disease-associated variants remains challenging due to the lack of relevant human experimental models. In recent years, reproductive organoids have emerged as powerful three-dimensional systems that recapitulate key structural, cellu
papers.summary: This review discusses how next-generation reproductive organoids—three-dimensional stem-cell-derived models of reproductive tissues—can be combined with genomics, multi-omics, and bioengineering approaches to study human infertility. The authors argue that these integrated platforms help overcome the limitations of traditional models by allowing functional testing of infertility-associated genetic variants and dissecting the complex genetic, epigenetic, and environmental contributors to the disorder.

papers.title: Integration of Single-Cell and Bulk RNA Sequencing Data to Identify Lactylation-Related Gene Signatures in Hepatic Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury Using Machine Learning Algorithms.
papers.abstract: Hepatic ischemia-reperfusion injury (HIRI) is not only a common complication of liver transplantation and major hepatic surgery but also a critical determinant of postoperative prognosis. Lactate metabolic reprogramming has been observed in HIRI, yet the role of lactate and its related lactylation in the pathogenesis of HIRI remains unclear. To address this, we integrated single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data with multiple bioinformatic approaches. Five single-cell gene set activity scoring methods (AUCell, UCell, singscore, ssGSEA, and AddModuleScore) were applied to evaluate lactylation activity
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing data to investigate lactylation-related gene signatures in hepatic ischemia-reperfusion injury (HIRI). Using five gene set activity scoring methods and machine learning algorithms, the authors identify lactylation-associated genes that may contribute to HIRI pathogenesis. The findings suggest lactate metabolism and lactylation play a role in HIRI, offering potential biomarkers or therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Integrated single-cell and bulk transcriptomic analysis reveals an epithelial cell-derived prognostic and immunotherapeutic signature with ADAM12 as a key functional regulator in non-small cell lung cancer.
papers.abstract: This study developed a Prognostic and Immunotherapeutic Signature (PIS) for NSCLC using single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data. By integrating TCGA and GEO datasets with machine learning, we identified key epithelial cells-related genes predictive of immunotherapy response. PIS effectively stratifies patients by survival and immune activity, with low-PIS individuals showing better outcomes and higher immune infiltration. We confirmed the high expression of ADAM12 in both tissue samples and cell lines, and validated its functional roles through cellular assays. Furthermore, mouse model experiments d
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data to build a prognostic and immunotherapeutic signature (PIS) for non-small cell lung cancer, based on epithelial cell-derived genes. The signature stratifies patients by survival and immune activity, and ADAM12 is identified and experimentally validated as a key functional regulator. The work links epithelial cell biology to immunotherapy response prediction in NSCLC.

papers.title: Machine learning identifies ac4C-related prognostic signature and TUBA1C as therapeutic target in COAD.
papers.abstract: To explore the role of N4-acetylcytidine (ac4C)-related genes (acRGs) in colon adenocarcinoma (COAD) and identify reliable prognostic biomarkers and potential therapeutic targets. Multi-source transcriptomic datasets (TCGA-COAD, GSE39582, GSE17536) and single-cell RNA-seq data were analyzed. Ten machine learning algorithms were integrated to construct an acRG-based prognostic signature (acRGBS). Immune microenvironment (TME) and genomic profiling were performed, with in vitro functional experiments validating TUBA1C's role. acRGBS, comprising four hub genes (SARAF, CDC42SE2, TSPYL2, TUBA1C), e
papers.journal: Mammalian genome : official journal of the International Mammalian Genome Society
papers.summary: This study used multi-source transcriptomic and single-cell RNA-seq data with ten integrated machine learning algorithms to build a prognostic signature based on N4-acetylcytidine (ac4C)-related genes in colon adenocarcinoma. The four-gene signature (SARAF, CDC42SE2, TSPYL2, TUBA1C) stratified patients by prognosis and was linked to immune microenvironment and genomic features, with in vitro experiments validating TUBA1C as a potential therapeutic target.

papers.title: Integrative single-cell and machine learning analysis identifies a tumor doubling time-related prognostic signature and therapeutic targets in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) exhibits marked molecular heterogeneity and diverse clinical outcomes, partly influenced by HPV status and the tumor immune microenvironment. Although tumor doubling time (TDT) reflects tumor growth kinetics and has prognostic relevance, its molecular basis in HNSCC remains unclear.
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell RNA sequencing with machine learning to identify a gene signature associated with tumor doubling time (TDT) in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma. The authors link this TDT-related signature to prognosis and propose potential therapeutic targets, while accounting for HPV status and the tumor immune microenvironment. The work suggests that tumor growth kinetics can be captured molecularly and may inform patient stratification.

papers.title: A systematic benchmark of bioinformatics methods for single-cell and spatial RNA-seq nanopore long reads data.
papers.abstract: Alternative splicing plays a crucial role in transcriptomic complexity, yet remains difficult to resolve at the single-cell level due to the limitations of short-read technologies. Coupling single-cell with long-read sequencing offers full-length transcript coverage, enabling more accurate isoform detection. Diverse computational tools tailored for single-cell and spatial long-read transcriptomics have been developed. To compare the effectiveness of these approaches, we generated paired short-read and Nanopore long-read single-cell datasets, tailored for benchmarking bioinformatics tools. We e
papers.summary: This paper presents a systematic benchmark of computational tools for analyzing single-cell and spatial RNA-seq data generated with Nanopore long-read sequencing. The authors created paired short-read and long-read single-cell datasets to evaluate how well different bioinformatics methods detect full-length transcripts and isoforms, addressing the challenge of resolving alternative splicing at single-cell resolution.

papers.title: Interpretable multi-omics integration across mixed-order tensors with MANTRA.
papers.abstract: The integration of multi-modal molecular data is crucial for understanding complex diseases, but existing methods struggle with modern experimental designs that generate datasets with mixed-order tensors-for example, a third-order drug-response tensor alongside a second-order transcriptomics matrix. Here, we present MANTRA (Multi-view ANalysis with Tensor and matRix Alignment), a probabilistic framework that integrates collections of tensors of different orders, combining the strengths of group factor analysis and tensor decomposition. MANTRA learns interpretable latent factors and naturally h
papers.summary: MANTRA is a probabilistic framework that integrates multi-omics datasets with mixed-order tensors, such as combining a third-order drug-response tensor with a second-order transcriptomics matrix. It learns interpretable latent factors by merging group factor analysis with tensor decomposition, enabling joint analysis of heterogeneous experimental designs.

papers.title: Alignment-free integration of single-nucleus ATAC-seq across species with sPYce.
papers.abstract: Changes in gene regulation largely contribute to differences in cellular identities and phenotypes between species. Single-nucleus assays for transposase-accessible chromatin with sequencing (snATAC-seq) are an efficient strategy to identify putative gene regulatory elements and provide new insight into evolutionary divergence of regulatory programmes. However, no dedicated framework exists to integrate and compare snATAC-seq data across species, while methods designed for single-cell gene expression data have serious limitations. Here we present sPYce, a cross-species snATAC-seq integration m
papers.summary: sPYce is a new computational framework for integrating single-nucleus ATAC-seq data across species without requiring sequence alignment, addressing a gap since existing methods were designed for single-cell gene expression data. It enables direct comparison of chromatin accessibility and regulatory programs between species, offering new insight into the evolutionary divergence of gene regulation.

papers.title: COL1A1+ Epithelial Cells Orchestrate VEGFA-VEGFR Signaling in Endometritis Revealed by Single-Cell Analysis.
papers.abstract: Endometritis is linked to adverse reproductive outcomes, but epithelial programs in disease initiation and persistence remain unclear. We aimed to systematically define inflammation-associated epithelial states and regulation in endometritis using single-cell analysis.
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell analysis to characterize epithelial cell states in endometritis, identifying a COL1A1+ epithelial population that appears to drive VEGFA-VEGFR signaling during inflammation. The findings suggest these cells play a central role in disease initiation and persistence, offering potential targets for understanding endometritis pathology.

papers.title: Advances in single-cell and spatial multi-omics for plant development and stress responses.
papers.abstract: Recent advances in single-cell and spatial multi-omics have enabled high-resolution profiling of plant cellular heterogeneity and tissue organization. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) captures transcriptional variation across cell types and states, while single-nucleus ATAC sequencing (snATAC-seq) provides information on chromatin accessibility and regulatory elements. Spatial transcriptomics (ST) and spatial metabolomics preserve spatial context, enabling in situ mapping of molecular and metabolic features in plant tissues. This review summarizes experimental and computational approache
papers.summary: This review summarizes recent advances in single-cell and spatial multi-omics technologies applied to plant development and stress responses. It covers scRNA-seq for transcriptional heterogeneity, snATAC-seq for chromatin accessibility, and spatial transcriptomics and metabolomics for preserving spatial context in plant tissues. The review also discusses experimental and computational approaches enabling these high-resolution plant profiling studies.

papers.title: microRNAs as Regulators of the Immune Response and Their Potential Therapeutic Applications in Cancer.
papers.abstract: MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are small non-coding RNAs that have emerged as critical regulators of gene expression and key cellular processes in cancer, including tumor cell proliferation, survival, metastasis, and both innate and adaptive immune responses within the tumor microenvironment. Through their ability to modulate immune cell development, differentiation, polarization, antigen presentation, cytokine signaling and immune checkpoint expression, miRNAs play a vital role in shaping immune responses and represent attractive therapeutic candidates for remodeling the tumor immune microenvironment. Th
papers.summary: This review discusses how microRNAs regulate both innate and adaptive immune responses within the tumor microenvironment, influencing immune cell development, polarization, antigen presentation, cytokine signaling, and immune checkpoint expression. It highlights the therapeutic potential of targeting or delivering miRNAs to remodel the tumor immune microenvironment in cancer treatment.

papers.title: High-resolution spatial transcriptomics of irradiated submandibular glands treated with fortified fibrin hydrogels.
papers.abstract: Previous studies showed that fortified fibrin hydrogel (Ep-FH), generated by conjugating laminin-1 peptides (A99 and YIGSR) and growth factors (FGF7 and FGF10) to fibrin hydrogels, improves epithelial organization and secretory function in irradiated mouse submandibular glands (SMG). To define the cell type-specific mechanisms underlying these effects, we generated high-resolution spatial transcriptomic profiles using the Xenium Prime Mouse Pan Tissue and Pathways Panel (5,000 genes). Treatment with Ep-FH partially reactivated secretory- and polarity-related genes, shifted stromal and immune t
papers.summary: This study uses high-resolution spatial transcriptomics (Xenium) to map gene expression changes in irradiated mouse submandibular glands treated with a fortified fibrin hydrogel (Ep-FH). The treatment partially restored secretory and polarity-related gene programs and altered stromal and immune cell states, revealing cell-type-specific mechanisms behind the hydrogel's regenerative effects.

papers.title: Combined multi-omics profiling and machine learning analysis reveals that Bregs and RPS2 promote bone metastasis in nasopharyngeal carcinoma.
papers.abstract: The bone is the primary site of distant metastasis in patients with nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC), and bone metastasis (BM) significantly increases mortality. Deciphering the complex crosstalk between cancer cells and their tumor microenvironment (TME) is crucial for identifying therapeutic targets aimed at eliminating metastasis-initiating cells and preventing the establishment of overt metastases. Regulatory B cells (Bregs), a specialized B-cell subset endowed with potent immunosuppressive functions, play a pivotal regulatory role within the TME. However, their specific contributions, pheno
papers.summary: This study combines multi-omics profiling with machine learning to investigate how regulatory B cells (Bregs) and the ribosomal protein RPS2 contribute to bone metastasis in nasopharyngeal carcinoma. The authors identify Bregs and RPS2 as potential drivers of the metastatic process, suggesting they may serve as therapeutic targets to prevent bone metastasis.

papers.title: STC1 is associated with tumor progression and suppressive niches in laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma (LSCC) exhibits high recurrence and therapy resistance. We aimed to investigate the undefined role of Stanniocalcin-1 (STC1) in LSCC pathogenesis.
papers.summary: This study investigates the role of Stanniocalcin-1 (STC1) in laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma (LSCC), a cancer with high recurrence and therapy resistance. The authors associate STC1 expression with tumor progression and the formation of immunosuppressive niches, suggesting it may contribute to LSCC pathogenesis and serve as a potential therapeutic target.

papers.title: Diurnal Insulin Clearance and Circadian Metabolic Gene Signatures in MASLD: Integrative Multi-Dataset Physiological and Transcriptomic Analysis.
papers.abstract: Insulin clearance is a key determinant of circulating insulin availability, but its diurnal variation and relationship with circadian metabolic programs in metabolic dysfunction associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) remain unclear. This study aimed to explore diurnal insulin clearance in humans and examine associated metabolic gene signatures in MASLD.
papers.summary: This study investigates how insulin clearance varies across the day and how this relates to circadian metabolic gene expression programs in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). Using integrative multi-dataset physiological and transcriptomic analyses, the authors identify diurnal patterns in insulin clearance and associated circadian metabolic gene signatures in MASLD.

papers.title: Integrative computational analysis of public fecal lipidomics and transcriptomics datasets suggests a candidate association between the COX-2 pathway and CE(20:4) in colorectal adenoma-carcinoma progression.
papers.abstract: The fecal lipidomic changes underlying the colorectal adenoma-carcinoma sequence remain incompletely characterized, particularly regarding the continuous metabolic trajectory and heterogeneity of precancerous adenomas. We aimed to use publicly available multi-omics data and an integrative computational framework to identify candidate lipidomic features associated with a CRC-like metabolic state in adenomas.
papers.summary: This study integrates publicly available fecal lipidomics and transcriptomics datasets to identify lipidomic features associated with a colorectal cancer-like metabolic state in precancerous adenomas. The authors propose a candidate link between the COX-2 pathway and the cholesteryl ester CE(20:4) along the adenoma-carcinoma progression sequence. The findings are computational and hypothesis-generating rather than experimentally validated.

papers.title: Integrative transcriptomic analysis of peripheral blood identifies NETosis-associated programs and a stratified adaptive immune suppression pattern in severe acute pancreatitis.
papers.abstract: Severe acute pancreatitis (SAP) is associated with persistent organ failure and substantial mortality, yet the transcriptomic mechanisms underlying progression from mild acute pancreatitis to severe-spectrum disease remain incompletely defined. Early identification of patients at risk of persistent organ failure remains an important unmet clinical need.
papers.summary: This study uses integrative transcriptomic analysis of peripheral blood to identify NETosis-associated gene programs and a stratified pattern of adaptive immune suppression in patients with severe acute pancreatitis. The findings suggest that blood-based transcriptomic signatures could help distinguish patients at risk of persistent organ failure from those with milder disease.

papers.title: scLTF: A self-training clustering framework for large-scale single-cell RNA-Seq data.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) technology has rapidly advanced in recent years, driving significant breakthroughs in developmental biology, cancer research, immunology, and other related fields. However, existing clustering methods still face performance bottlenecks when handling large-scale scRNA-seq data. To address this challenge, we propose a self-training clustering method for large-scale single-cell RNA-seq data, termed scLTF (Single-cell Louvain-Transformer Framework for Large-scale Clustering). This method first generates preliminary clusters using a fast Louvain algorithm and
papers.summary: scLTF is a self-training clustering framework for large-scale scRNA-seq data that combines a fast Louvain algorithm for initial clustering with a Transformer-based model to refine cluster assignments. The approach aims to overcome performance bottlenecks of existing methods when handling very large single-cell datasets.

papers.title: Single-cell-informed senescence programs underpin a machine-learning prognostic model robustly validated across melanoma cohorts.
papers.abstract: Cellular senescence (CS) shapes tumor evolution and the tumor microenvironment (TME), yet senescence-informed prognostic models for skin cutaneous melanoma (SKCM) remain limited. We aimed to develop and validate a robust senescence-related prognostic signature by integrating single-cell and bulk transcriptomic data with systematic machine-learning screening.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and bulk transcriptomic data to define senescence-related gene programs in skin cutaneous melanoma and uses machine-learning screening to build a prognostic signature. The resulting model is validated across multiple independent melanoma cohorts, linking senescence programs to tumor evolution and the tumor microenvironment.

papers.title: Multi-omics and machine learning reveal LYZ and ISG15 as diagnostic and therapeutic targets in autoimmune-mediated chronic kidney disease.
papers.abstract: CKD represents a substantial worldwide health challenge, defined by the gradual development of tubulointerstitial fibrosis and reduced renal performance. Autoimmune-mediated factors are central to this pathological process, yet early diagnostic biomarkers and specific therapeutic targets are scarce. The objective of this research is to systematically pinpoint crucial specific genes that contribute to autoimmune-mediated CKD progression.
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data with machine learning to identify LYZ and ISG15 as key genes involved in autoimmune-mediated chronic kidney disease. These genes are proposed as potential diagnostic biomarkers and therapeutic targets, addressing the current lack of early detection markers and specific treatments for this condition.

papers.title: Identification and Validation of a Two-Gene NK Cell-Related Risk Model for COPD: Integration of Single-Cell and Bulk RNA-Seq Analysis.
papers.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) involves chronic inflammation with potential involvement of natural killer (NK) cells, but NK cell-related diagnostic markers remain limited. This study aimed to identify NK cell-related hub genes and construct a risk model for COPD.
papers.journal: International journal of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data to identify natural killer (NK) cell-related hub genes in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and builds a two-gene risk model for the disease. The authors validate this model as a potential diagnostic tool, highlighting NK cell involvement in COPD pathogenesis.

papers.title: Multi-omics mapping of PSC genetic risk to a high TWAS-active JAML+ lipid-associated macrophage program: bridging single-cell heterogeneity, spatial fibrotic niches, and machine learning selection.
papers.abstract: Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) is a chronic cholestatic liver disease with progressive peribiliary inflammation and fibrosis. Disease-modifying therapies are lacking, and the cell-type-specific mechanisms linking genetic susceptibility to pathogenic immune states remain incompletely understood.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data to map primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) genetic risk variants to a specific macrophage population characterized by JAML expression and lipid-associated gene programs, using transcriptome-wide association study (TWAS) approaches. The authors combine single-cell heterogeneity analysis, spatial profiling of fibrotic niches, and machine learning to identify this JAML+ lipid-associated macrophage program as a key pathogenic cell state linked to PSC susceptibility. The work bridges genetic risk to cell-type-specific immune mechanisms in PSC, nominating a potential target population for future therapeutic development.

papers.title: A Hypoxia Associated STC2 High Endothelial Subpopulation is Linked to Lipid Metabolic Reprogramming, Pathological Angiogenesis, and Immune Remodeling in Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Hypoxia drives malignant advancement and immune escape in HNSCC, but its cell‑type‑specific regulatory circuitry within the TME remains insufficiently elucidated. This study systematically characterizes hypoxia‑associated molecular programs and identifies core genes with relevance to prognosis and therapeutic response.
papers.summary: This study characterizes hypoxia-associated molecular programs in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) and identifies a STC2-high endothelial subpopulation linked to lipid metabolic reprogramming, pathological angiogenesis, and immune remodeling. The authors highlight core genes with potential prognostic and therapeutic relevance, suggesting cell-type-specific hypoxia responses within the tumor microenvironment.

papers.title: Multiscale characterization of an inflammatory macrophage state associated with an air pollutant-prioritized prognostic signature in gastric cancer.
papers.abstract: Air pollutants are implicated in carcinogenesis, but their relevance to gastric cancer (GC) across prognosis, tumor organization and cell behavior remains unclear. We integrated evidence to evaluate pollutant-prioritized GC candidates.
papers.summary: This study integrates air pollution exposure data with gastric cancer molecular profiling to build a pollutant-prioritized prognostic signature, then characterizes an inflammatory macrophage state linked to that signature across tumor organization and cellular behavior. The work suggests that pollutant-associated signals may shape the tumor microenvironment and prognosis in gastric cancer.

papers.title: Spatially convergent functional MRI signatures of diabetes and male sex identify genetic vulnerabilities to accelerated brain ageing.
papers.abstract: Age-related cognitive decline results from complex interactions between neuroendocrine and neurometabolic processes that undergo lifelong degradation, yet the mechanisms underlying these interactions remain poorly understood. This study examined the effects of diabetes and sex on functional brain networks across ageing through analysis of two large cohorts (N = 1621 total) using both 3T and 7T functional MRI, complemented by spatial transcriptomic data from over 14 000 genes from six post-mortem brains. Four networks-cingulo-opercular, default mode, salience and lateral somatomotor-exhibited s
papers.summary: This study combined functional MRI from two large cohorts (N=1621) with spatial transcriptomic data from post-mortem brains to examine how diabetes and male sex interact to affect brain ageing. Four functional networks showed convergent signatures linked to these factors, and the spatial gene expression patterns identified genetic vulnerabilities associated with accelerated brain ageing.

papers.title: Identification and experimental validation of CCL26 as a core comorbid gene and biomarker for atopic dermatitis and allergic asthma via machine learning and multi-omics analysis.
papers.abstract: Atopic dermatitis (AD) and allergic asthma (AA) frequently co-occur and are a core component of the "atopic march." However, the shared molecular mechanisms linking these conditions, as well as the core comorbid genes with diagnostic value, remain poorly understood.
papers.summary: This study uses machine learning and multi-omics analysis to identify CCL26 as a shared core gene and potential biomarker linking atopic dermatitis and allergic asthma, two conditions that frequently co-occur in the 'atopic march.' The authors experimentally validate CCL26, suggesting it may serve as a diagnostic biomarker and therapeutic target for these comorbid allergic diseases.

papers.title: Genetic associations link lung cancer liability to brain imaging phenotypes and nominate an FN1-associated tumor-oligodendrocyte program in small-cell lung cancer.
papers.abstract: Brain metastasis is a major cause of mortality in lung cancer, particularly in small-cell lung cancer (SCLC). Whether genetic susceptibility to lung cancer is associated with brain structural and functional traits relevant to metastatic vulnerability remains unclear. We investigated subtype-specific genetic associations with brain imaging phenotypes and explored the biological context of the SCLC-associated white-matter signal.
papers.summary: This study uses genetic association analysis to link inherited lung cancer susceptibility, especially small-cell lung cancer (SCLC), to brain imaging phenotypes such as white-matter structure. The authors identify an FN1-associated tumor-oligodendrocyte program that may contribute to brain metastatic vulnerability in SCLC.

papers.title: Circulating and tumor-infiltrating immune cell profiles in cervical cancer checkpoint blockade: multi-omics biomarkers of response and resistance.
papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint blockade has changed the therapeutic landscape of cervical cancer, but clinical benefit remains heterogeneous and difficult to predict with single biomarkers. Cervical cancer is a particularly suitable setting for immune-cell profiling because HPV-driven antigenicity, chemoradiotherapy-induced tissue remodeling, anti-angiogenic combinations, and repeated exposure to PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors all shape the blood-tumor immune axis. This Mini Review discusses how circulating immune cells and tumor-infiltrating immune cells can be jointly interrogated by multi-omics technologies to i
papers.summary: This mini review discusses how combining circulating immune cell profiling with tumor-infiltrating immune cell analysis via multi-omics technologies could improve prediction of response and resistance to immune checkpoint blockade in cervical cancer. It highlights that HPV-driven antigenicity, chemoradiotherapy, anti-angiogenic combinations, and repeated PD-1/PD-L1 exposure all shape the blood-tumor immune axis, making single biomarkers insufficient. The authors argue for integrated multi-omics biomarker strategies in this clinical setting.
